title: autotune: cost-optimization defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Samir Patel
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost for typical production workloads by making safer, opinionated defaults for batching and KV/prefix caching, exposing quantization profiles for model variants, and adding a small unit-economics toolkit to the console/CLI to validate savings before rollout. Scope: runtime defaults + heuristics, model profile metadata, console UI/CLI hooks for unit-econ simulations, migration for existing deployment configs, tests, and docs. Summary of changes: - Adds autotune defaults module (runtime/scheduler/autotune_defaults.py) that computes batch size targets and cache TTL heuristics based on recent request histograms and SLO constraints. Defaults are conservative and opt into aggressive profiles only when steady-state confidence is high. - Introduces quantization profile registry (model-registry/quant_profiles.yaml + loader) to declare recommended quant levels per model family/size and expected perf/cost deltas. - Adds unit-econ simulation endpoint and CLI flag (console/api/unit_econ_simulate and redwoodctl unit-econ) which computes expected cost/latency tradeoffs given a customer workload sample. - Runtime changes to apply defaults when no custom config is present; existing explicit configs are preserved. Migration notes included. Testing & validation: unit tests for heuristics, integration tests exercising end-to-end simulation, Canaries ran against perf-canary with 50% synthetic traffic for 48 hours. Observability: new metrics (autotune.confidence, autotune.applied_profile, unit_econ.estimated_saving) and dashboard updates. Checklist:
- [x] Implementation + unit tests
- [x] Integration tests + perf canary run
- [x] Docs & console UI text updates
- [x] Telemetry and alerting for misestimated savings
- [x] Backwards-compatible: existing explicit configs unchanged

Migration: On deploy, runtime will log deployments without explicit batching/caching configs and apply conservative defaults. Admins can opt-out by setting config.autotune.enabled=false. Follow-ups: automated A/B rollout (ENG-4990), guardrail rules in RBAC (ENG-5053).

review_comments: Priya Raman (2025-11-04): Please add a short explanation of the confidence scoring and how it decays on traffic shifts. Also request telemetry for false-positive savings.
Author reply (2025-11-05): Added confidence scoring docstring and emitted unit_econ.confidence metric. Updated tests to simulate traffic shift and confidence decay.
Lina Zhang (2025-11-06): Can we avoid applying aggressive quant profiles automatically? Suggest require 7-day steady-state or explicit opt-in for >8-bit quantization.
Author reply (2025-11-07): Agree. Modified autotune_defaults to only enable aggressive quant profiles when confidence > 0.95 and steady_state_window >= 7d. Added CLI override for testing.
Ethan Cole (2025-11-09): Integration run showed a flaky test related to deterministic RNG in the perf harness; small fix proposed.
Author reply (2025-11-10): Fixed RNG seed in perf harness and re-ran the canary; metrics stable, no regressed latency observed.
ci_checks: integration-tests: failed (flaky perf test) -> fixed and re-run -> passed
release_notes: Adds conservative autotune defaults for batching and KV/prefix caching, introduces quantization profile registry, and a unit-economics simulation tool in Console/CLI. Defaults are opt-out and guarded by confidence heuristics. Intended to reduce per-token costs while preserving latency SLOs.
notes: Backwards compatible: explicit customer configs are unchanged.
Follow-ups: ENG-4990 automated A/B rollout, ENG-5053 RBAC guardrails for sensitive model families.
